037/**
038 * Parent class for all Juneau serializers.
039 *
040 * <h5 class='topic'>Description</h5>
041 * <p>
042 * Base serializer class that serves as the parent class for all serializers.
043 *
044 * <p>
045 * The purpose of this class is:
046 * <ul>
047 *    <li>Maintain a read-only configuration state of a serializer.
048 *    <li>Create session objects used for serializing POJOs (i.e. {@link SerializerSession}).
049 *    <li>Provide convenience methods for serializing POJOs without having to construct session objects.
050 * </ul>
051 *
052 * <p>
053 * Subclasses should (but are not required to) extend directly from {@link OutputStreamSerializer} or {@link WriterSerializer} depending on
054 * whether it's a stream or character based serializer.
055 *
056 * <p>
057 * Subclasses must implement serialization via one of the following methods:
058 * <ul class='javatree'>
059 *    <li class='jmp'>{@link #doWrite(SerializerSession, SerializerPipe, Object)}
060 *    <li class='jmp'>{@link SerializerSession#doWrite(SerializerPipe, Object)}
061 * </ul>
062 * <br>
063 *
064 * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
065 *    <li class='note'>This class is thread safe and reusable.
066 * </ul>
067 *
068 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
069 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/SerializersAndParsers">Serializers and Parsers</a>
070
071 * </ul>
072 */
073@SuppressWarnings({
074   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
075   "rawtypes" // createSerializerBuilder() returns the raw Builder because the concrete SELF type is only known reflectively via Context.createBuilder(c)
076})

174      /**
175       *    Specifies the accept media types that the serializer can handle.
176       *
177       *    <p>
178       *    Can contain meta-characters per the <c>media-type</c> specification of <a class="doclink" href="https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html">RFC2616/14.1</a>
179       *    <p>
180       *    If empty, then assumes the only media type supported is <c>produces</c>.
181       *    <p>
182       *    For example, if this serializer produces <js>"application/json"</js> but should handle media types of
183       *    <js>"application/json"</js> and <js>"text/json"</js>, then the arguments should be:
184       *    <p class='bjava'>
185       *       <jv>builder</jv>.produces(<js>"application/json"</js>);
186       *       <jv>builder</jv>.accept(<js>"application/json,text/json"</js>);
187       *    </p>
188       * <p>
189       * The accept value can also contain q-values.
190       *
191       * @param value The value for this setting.
192       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (will default to the value specified by {@link #produces(String)}).
193       * @return This object.
194       */
195      public SELF accept(String value) {
196         accept = value;
197         return self();
198      }
199
200      /**
201       * Add <js>"_type"</js> properties when needed.
202       *
203       * <p>
204       * When enabled, <js>"_type"</js> properties will be added to beans if their type cannot be inferred
205       * through reflection.
206       *
207       * <p>
208       * This is used to recreate the correct objects during parsing if the object types cannot be inferred.
209       * <br>For example, when serializing a <c>Map&lt;String,Object&gt;</c> field where the bean class cannot be determined from
210       * the type of the values.
211       *
212       * <p>
213       * Note the differences between the following settings:
214       * <ul class='javatree'>
215       *    <li class='jf'>{@link #addRootType()} - Affects whether <js>'_type'</js> is added to root node.
216       *    <li class='jf'>{@link #addBeanTypes()} - Affects whether <js>'_type'</js> is added to any nodes.
217       * </ul>
218       *
219       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
220       * <p class='bjava'>
221       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that adds _type to nodes.</jc>
222       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
223       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
224       *       .addBeanTypes()
225       *       .build();
226       *
227       *    <jc>// Our map of beans to serialize.</jc>
228       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"mybean"</js>)
229       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
230       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
231       *    }
232       *    JsonMap <jv>myMap</jv> = JsonMap.of(<js>"foo"</js>, <jk>new</jk> MyBean());
233       *
234       *    <jc>// Will contain:  {"foo":{"_type":"mybean","foo":"bar"}}</jc>
235       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jv>myMap</jv>);
236       * </p>
237       *
238       * <p>
239       * <b>Token streams:</b> the cursor's raw structural methods do not emit <c>"_type"</c>;
240       * however this setting IS honored by
241       * {@link TokenWriter#object(Object) TokenWriter.object(Object)}
242       * when walking a bean.
243       *
244       * @return This object.
245       */
246      public SELF addBeanTypes() {
247         return addBeanTypes(true);
248      }
249
250      /**
251       * Same as {@link #addBeanTypes()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
252       *
253       * @param value The value for this setting.
254       * @return This object.
255       */
256      public SELF addBeanTypes(boolean value) {
257         addBeanTypes = value;
258         return self();
259      }
260
261      /**
262       * Add type attribute to root nodes.
263       *
264       * <p>
265       * When enabled, <js>"_type"</js> properties will be added to top-level beans.
266       *
267       * <p>
268       * When disabled, it is assumed that the parser knows the exact Java POJO type being parsed, and therefore top-level
269       * type information that might normally be included to determine the data type will not be serialized.
270       *
271       * <p>
272       * For example, when serializing a top-level POJO with a {@link Marshalled#typeName() @Marshalled(typeName)} value, a
273       * <js>'_type'</js> attribute will only be added when this setting is enabled.
274       *
275       * <p>
276       * Note the differences between the following settings:
277       * <ul class='javatree'>
278       *    <li class='jf'>{@link #addRootType()} - Affects whether <js>'_type'</js> is added to root node.
279       *    <li class='jf'>{@link #addBeanTypes()} - Affects whether <js>'_type'</js> is added to any nodes.
280       * </ul>
281       *
282       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
283       * <p class='bjava'>
284       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that adds _type to root node.</jc>
285       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv>= JsonSerializer
286       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
287       *       .addRootType()
288       *       .build();
289       *
290       *    <jc>// Our bean to serialize.</jc>
291       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"mybean"</js>)
292       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
293       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
294       *    }
295       *
296       *    <jc>// Will contain:  {"_type":"mybean","foo":"bar"}</jc>
297       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
298       * </p>
299       *
300       * <p>
301       * <b>Token streams:</b> the cursor's raw structural methods do not emit <c>"_type"</c>;
302       * however this setting IS honored by
303       * {@link TokenWriter#object(Object) TokenWriter.object(Object)}
304       * for the root value.
305       *
306       * @return This object.
307       */
308      public SELF addRootType() {
309         return addRootType(true);
310      }
311
312      /**
313       * Same as {@link #addRootType()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
314       *
315       * @param value The value for this setting.
316       * @return This object.
317       */
318      public SELF addRootType(boolean value) {
319         addRootType = value;
320         return self();
321      }
322

325         return build(Serializer.class);
326      }

350            produces,
351            accept,
352            addBeanTypes,
353            addRootType,

356            sortCollections,
357            sortMaps,
358            trimEmptyCollections,
359            trimEmptyMaps,
360            trimStrings,
361            uriContext,
362            uriRelativity,
363            uriResolution,
364            listener
365         );
366         // @formatter:on
367      }

369      /**
370       * Don't trim null bean property values.
371       *
372       * <p>
373       * When enabled, null bean values will be serialized to the output.
374       *
375       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
376       *    <li class='note'>Not enabling this setting will cause <c>Map</c>s with <jk>null</jk> values to be lost during parsing.
377       * </ul>
378       *
379       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
380       * <p class='bjava'>
381       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that serializes null properties.</jc>
382       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
383       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
384       *       .keepNullProperties()
385       *       .build();
386       *
387       *    <jc>// Our bean to serialize.</jc>
388       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
389       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <jk>null</jk>;
390       *    }
391       *
392       *    <jc>// Will contain "{foo:null}".</jc>
393       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
394       * </p>
395       *
396       * <p>
397       * <b>Token streams:</b> the cursor's raw structural methods always emit what the caller
398       * asks for; however this setting IS honored by
399       * {@link TokenWriter#object(Object) TokenWriter.object(Object)}
400       * during a bean walk.
401       *
402       * @return This object.
403       */
404      public SELF keepNullProperties() {
405         return keepNullProperties(true);
406      }
407
408      /**
409       * Same as {@link #keepNullProperties()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
410       *
411       * @param value The value for this setting.
412       * @return This object.
413       */
414      public SELF keepNullProperties(boolean value) {
415         keepNullProperties = value;
416         return self();
417      }
418
419      /**
420       * Don't serialize bean properties whose values equal the default for their type.
421       *
422       * <p>
423       * When enabled, bean properties whose current value equals the type's natural default are omitted from
424       * the serialized output. This is the Juneau analog of Jackson's <c>JsonInclude.Include.NON_DEFAULT</c>
425       * inclusion mode.
426       *
427       * <p>
428       * The notion of "default" depends on the property type:
429       * <ul class='spaced-list'>
430       *    <li>Primitives and primitive wrappers (<code><jk>int</jk></code>, <code>Integer</code>,
431       *       <code><jk>boolean</jk></code>, <code>Boolean</code>, etc.) use the Java type default
432       *       (<c>0</c>, <c>false</c>, <code>'\0'</code>, <jk>null</jk>).
433       *    <li>Bean properties on bean-typed property values use a <i>reference instance</i> of the bean type —
434       *       instantiated once via the no-arg constructor and cached on the {@link ClassMeta} — and the
435       *       property is omitted when its current value equals that reference's value.
436       *    <li>When no reference instance can be built (no accessible no-arg constructor, or instantiation
437       *       throws), <c>nonDefault</c> is silently skipped for that bean — the property is emitted normally
438       *       rather than failing the serialize.
439       * </ul>
440       *
441       * <p>
442       * <b>Equality semantics:</b> value-equals-default uses {@link Objects#equals}, with numeric values
443       * compared by mathematical value (BigDecimal.compareTo-style) so <c>1.0</c> equals <c>1</c>,
444       * <c>0.0</c> equals <c>-0.0</c>, and <code>BigDecimal(<js>"1.0"</js>)</code> equals
445       * <code>BigDecimal(<js>"1"</js>)</code>.
446       *
447       * <p>
448       * <b>Precedence:</b> the serialize-side inclusion knobs short-circuit in a fixed order — first "omit" wins:
449       * <ol>
450       *    <li><jk>null</jk> values (including {@link Optional#empty()}) are governed by
451       *       {@link #keepNullProperties()}.
452       *    <li>Non-<jk>null</jk> string values are normalized by {@link #trimStrings()}.
453       *    <li>Empty collections / arrays / maps are omitted by {@link #trimEmptyCollections()} /
454       *       {@link #trimEmptyMaps()}.
455       *    <li>Surviving values that equal their type's default are omitted by <c>nonDefault</c>.
456       * </ol>
457       * <jk>null</jk> is resolved by <c>keepNullProperties</c>, not treated as a <c>nonDefault</c> case.
458       *
459       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
460       * <p class='bjava'>
461       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that omits default-valued properties.</jc>
462       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
463       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
464       *       .nonDefault()
465       *       .build();
466       *
467       *    <jc>// Our bean to serialize.</jc>
468       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
469       *       <jk>public int</jk> <jf>count</jf>;            <jc>// Default 0; omitted unless set to non-zero.</jc>
470       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>name</jf> = <js>"x"</js>; <jc>// Bean-default is "x"; only omitted when value equals "x".</jc>
471       *    }
472       *
473       *    <jc>// Produces "{}" because both fields equal their defaults.</jc>
474       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
475       * </p>
476       *
477       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
478       *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NullAndInclusionPolicies">Null & Inclusion Policies</a>
479       * </ul>
480       *
481       * @return This object.
482       * @since 10.0.0
483       */
484      public SELF nonDefault() {
485         return nonDefault(true);
486      }
487
488      /**
489       * Same as {@link #nonDefault()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
490       *
491       * @param value The value for this setting.
492       * @return This object.
493       * @since 10.0.0
494       */
495      public SELF nonDefault(boolean value) {
496         nonDefault = value;
497         return self();
498      }

500      /**
501       * Serializer listener.
502       *
503       * <p>
504       * Class used to listen for errors and warnings that occur during serialization.
505       *
506       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
507       * <p class='bjava'>
508       *    <jc>// Define our serializer listener.</jc>
509       *    <jc>// Simply captures all errors.</jc>
510       *    <jk>public class</jk> MySerializerListener <jk>extends</jk> SerializerListener {
511       *
512       *       <jc>// A simple property to store our events.</jc>
513       *       <jk>public</jk> List&lt;String&gt; <jf>events</jf> = <jk>new</jk> LinkedList&lt;&gt;();
514       *
515       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
516       *       <jk>public</jk> &lt;T&gt; <jk>void</jk> onError(SerializerSession <jv>session</jv>, Throwable <jv>throwable</jv>, String <jv>msg</jv>) {
517       *          <jf>events</jf>.add(<jv>session</jv>.getLastLocation() + <js>","</js> + <jv>msg</jv> + <js>","</js> + <jv>throwable</jv>);
518       *       }
519       *    }
520       *
521       *    <jc>// Create a serializer using our listener.</jc>
522       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
523       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
524       *       .listener(MySerializerListener.<jk>class</jk>)
525       *       .build();
526       *
527       *    <jc>// Create a session object.</jc>
528       *    <jc>// Needed because listeners are created per-session.</jc>
529       *    <jk>try</jk> (WriterSerializerSession <jv>session</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.createSession()) {
530       *
531       *       <jc>// Serialize a bean.</jc>
532       *       String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
533       *
534       *       <jc>// Get the listener.</jc>
535       *       MySerializerListener <jv>listener</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.getListener(MySerializerListener.<jk>class</jk>);
536       *
537       *       <jc>// Dump the results to the console.</jc>
538       *       Json5.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.println(<jv>listener</jv>.<jf>events</jf>);
539       *    }
540       * </p>
541       *
542       * <p>
543       * <b>Token streams:</b> this setting is not honored by {@link TokenWritable#writeTokens(Object) writeTokens}
544       * &mdash; listeners are POJO-level observers with no token-layer analog.
545       *
546       * @param value
547       *    The new value for this property.
548       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (no listener will be used, listener methods will not be called).
549       * @return This object.
550       */
551      public SELF listener(Class<? extends SerializerListener> value) {
552         listener = value;
553         return self();
554      }
555
556      /**
557       * Specifies the media type that this serializer produces.
558       *
559       * @param value The value for this setting.
560       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (clears the produces media type).
561       * @return This object.
562       */
563      public SELF produces(String value) {
564         produces = value;
565         return self();
566      }

568      /**
569       * Sort arrays and collections alphabetically.
570       *
571       * <p>
572       * When enabled, copies and sorts the contents of arrays and collections before serializing them.
573       *
574       * <p>
575       * Note that this introduces a performance penalty since it requires copying the existing collection.
576       *
577       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
578       * <p class='bjava'>
579       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that sorts arrays and collections before serialization.</jc>
580       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
581       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
582       *       .sortCollections()
583       *       .build();
584       *
585       *    <jc>// An unsorted array</jc>
586       *    String[] <jv>myArray</jv> = {<js>"foo"</js>,<js>"bar"</js>,<js>"baz"</js>};
587       *
588       *    <jc>// Produces ["bar","baz","foo"]</jc>
589       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jv>myArray</jv>);
590       * </p>
591       *
592       * <p>
593       * <b>Token streams:</b> the cursor's raw structural methods emit elements in the order the
594       * caller emits them.  This setting IS honored by

828       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()

830       *       .uriRelativity(<jsf>RESOURCE</jsf>)  <jc>// Assume relative paths are relative to servlet.</jc>
831       *       .uriResolution(<jsf>ABSOLUTE</jsf>)  <jc>// Serialize URLs as absolute paths.</jc>
832       *       .build();

834       *    <jc>// A relative URL</jc>

837       *    <jc>// Produces "http://localhost:10000/myContext/myServlet/foo/bar"</jc>

841       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
